subject: Krypton Health stream choke / WebSocket timeouts — rapid mitigation plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kryptonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T13:12:00-08:00
Subject: Krypton Health — intermittent stream choke during overnight batch

Hi Laura,

We're seeing repeated WebSocket timeouts and long pauses (10–30s) in the streaming responses during our overnight inference job that runs large batch requests against the Redwood hosted endpoint. Impact: our downstream transcription pipeline drops segments and we get partial transcripts — customer SLA at risk.

Symptoms observed (last 12 hours):
- Multiple 504/ETIMEDOUTs in client telemetry around 02:00–03:30 PT.
- Server response stream shows long gaps between token frames; client sees socket still open but no chunks for 12–28s.
- Error rate spike from ~0.2% -> 4.6% during peak.
- Throughput drop ~35% compared to baseline.

We captured a short ws capture and server logs attached (krypton_logs_1129.tar.gz). Can you triage? This is affecting 3 pilot hospitals — want to avoid escalation to their CIO.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Krypton Health
ops@kryptonhealth.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kryptonhealth.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Krypton Health — intermittent stream choke during overnight batch

Hi Samir — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. We've opened an internal triage and I’ve looped in David (SRE) and Vanessa (realtime infra lead).

Immediate ask: can you paste a short HTTP/WebSocket request id from one of the failed sessions (x-request-id or request-id header) and confirm whether you were using the pooled session (keep-alive) or creating a new socket per job? That will help with correlating proxies.

We’ll prioritize this with the war room and keep you updated every 2 hours until resolved. Proposed immediate mitigations we may ask you to try: temporarily reduce parallel connections to 8, enable a 15s client-side keepalive, and send any pcap or full socket capture.

Attaching an internal incident tracker and will follow with a technical write-up.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwoods Inference
From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-28T15:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Krypton Health — intermittent stream choke during overnight batch

Laura / team,

I pulled the logs from the attachment. Quick notes from initial triage:
- Proxy and upstream logs show sustained write stalls to the backend GPU pods starting at 02:08 PT — request latencies jump but backend (model) CPU/GPU looks nominal.
- The nginx/proxy connection queues show backlog growth and then abrupt draining with many connections still open (suggests backpressure or socket-level stalls rather than HTTP 500s).
- I see a burst of TLS record retransmits and a handful of TCP window updates which align with your 'socket open but no chunks' symptom.

Hypothesis: we’re hitting a transfer window/keepalive misalignment combined with a bursty throughput profile that overwhelms proxy buffering. Possible contributing factors: aggressive client parallelism, proxy queue configuration for chunk flushing, or intermittent GC in the service side code path that pauses token emission for tens of seconds.

Next steps I’ll run: recreate a high-throughput replay in staging using the provided request shapes, capture pprof of the streaming worker, and validate proxy socket timeouts. Can the customer reproduce with a lightweight replay? Samir, if you can run an abridged repro at lower RPS but same concurrency pattern that helps us reproduce quicker.

I’m marking this P1 and will post findings to the ticket (KH-1122).

— David
David Kim
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kryptonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@kryptonhealth.com
Date: 2026-11-29T07:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Krypton Health — intermittent stream choke during overnight batch

Thanks David — we ran an isolated replay at 50% of our overnight traffic and reproduced a 12s token gap twice. Request-ids pasted below: request-id=KH-20261129-7b9a, request-id=KH-20261129-7f2d. Attached the full tcpdump and a screenshot of the client timeline (ws_capture_1129.png).

We’re happy to run any config changes you recommend, but the pilot hospitals are asking for a guaranteed window during their maintenance window tomorrow afternoon. Appreciate fast turnaround.

Samir
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-29T10:04:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Krypton — proposed immediate mitigations and exec note

Team — summary and recommended immediate mitigations (for exec / customer-facing steps):
1) Short-term customer mitigations (can be applied in minutes):
   - Ask customer to cap concurrent sockets to 8 and enable a 15s TCP keepalive from client side.
   - Enable chunk-flush heuristics on the proxy for the affected route (reduce proxy buffering window from 8KB -> 2KB).
2) Platform-side mitigation (requires deploy, target 2–4 hours):
   - Roll a config update to increase socket write timeout and enable aggressive write flush for streaming routes.
   - Deploy a temporary rate-limiter to smooth bursts per-customer for the route.
3) Next-day action (root cause):
   - Instrument streaming workers with finer-grained pprof and GC tracing; validate we’re not seeing stall pauses in the emission loop.

Customer comms: Laura, propose this note to Samir: we have a short-term plan to reduce the risk during their maintenance window and will follow with a full RCA. Offer a goodwill credit for their pilot.

I’ll prepare a brief MAP (mutual_action_plan_krypton.xlsx) and an executive summary for CSM/AE to share.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Lead, Realtime Infra
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@kryptonhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-30T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Krypton Health — rapid mitigations and call scheduled for 2026-11-30 13:00 PT

Samir — short update and plan for today:

1) Immediate mitigations we recommend you apply now (low-risk):
   - Cap concurrent sockets to 8 per host and enable 15s TCP keepalive on your side.
   - If possible, throttle burst dispatches by smoothing the inter-request interval by 100–250ms.

2) Platform actions (in progress):
   - We’ve applied a proxy config change in the canary pool to reduce buffer coalescing for your tenant.
   - David’s team is running a targeted replay in staging to validate the write-flush change; early signs look promising.

3) Call: scheduled with our engineering leads at 13:00 PT today to walk through findings and run a controlled replay with you. Invited: Samir, ops, David, Vanessa, Grace (CSM).

We’ll also include a goodwill credit proposal in the call. Thank you for the detailed logs — that sped up triage.

Best,
Laura Bennett
